“In the case comments, the original device was showing offline. The customer had already swapped out the GRS-5 for the GRS-7 and the RCB that was already in the room. No software faults found. where it the value seems to be consistently populated rather than in the Staff record. As a work around I updated the StaffTitleId to match the TitleId  
in the staff table and triggered a full process of the ETL so that data will be pulled into the model. I also add a small trigger to the table so that  
any inserts or updates to the staff record will automatically sync the StaffTitleId with the TitleId.

This is a change that should be implemented for ERM+ so that other customer do not experience the missing filteing on the handleful of ERM+ reports.

root_cause_summary: The combination of the removing i2c commands sent to the device in the linux kernel driver when the nurse call application would startup or exit before reboot and the removing reset gpio being triggered at startup resolved the issue.  The gpio reset not successful resetting the touchscreen part seems to be a hardware flaw that can be worked around by this software modification.
investigation_details: The scenario where the device is rebooted remotely via the primary console or secondary console reboot rooms screen seems to put the touchscreen part into a state where it can’t be reset via the reset gpio pin.  During a soft or hard reboot the reset gpio is typically used to reset the device.

The driver also had some behaviors that could have contributed to getting the device in a state that would not allow it to reset.  There were several state changes that triggered i2c command being sent to the touchscreen controller when the nurse call application would start up and connect to the touch controller for event notification. 

Removing both the attempt to reset the touchscreen part with the gpio pin and the additional unnecessary commands being sent in the driver resolved the issue.

Before:  Touchscreen drivers were compiled into the linux kernel for the grs7 and grs10h.  And a gpio reset was defined for each touch screen controller driver for different hardware revs of the grs7 or grs10h.  Compiling the modules into the kernel caused them to be run one at a time at boot.

The atmel max touch driver used by the GRS7 hardware rev with part number P2594VNC7C11 will be attempted first.  And the gpio reset will not be used for the driver.  Using the gpio reset was determined to cause the issue.

comment_summary: Calls intermittently failed to clear from the Status board at sites running 4.1.200, severely enough that one customer paused remaining upgrade projects. Device Service Host logs for a stuck call showed the de-duplication logic failing to trigger, producing a SQL error 2601 "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'NCC.V_ActiveCall' with unique index 'AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'" so call creation was abandoned, after which every subsequent status update (Answered, Cancel) failed with SQL error 257 "Implicit conversion from data type nvarchar to timestamp is not allowed" and the call never cleared. The suspicion was that a secondary or monitoring console reports the alert with the same BaseCallID but a different RequestingDeviceId, causing IsDuplicateAlertNotification() in AlertMessageHandler.cs to fail, and the affected units all used secondary consoles and unit monitoring. A separate bug was also found in the call_update stored procedure, where the row edition check compares @RowEdition to itself rather than to the stored RowEdition. The workaround that resolved it was setting MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads to 1 in the Device Service appsettings.json file, after which no further stuck-call reports were made at either site.

summary: When a GRS7 hardware revision with part number P2594VNC7C11 is soft rebooted in some cases the touchscreen does not accept touch input.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  Touchscreen drivers were compiled into the linux kernel for the grs7 and grs10h.  And a gpio reset was defined for each touch screen controller driver for different hardware revs of the grs7 or grs10h.  Compiling the modules into the kernel caused them to be run one at a time at boot.  
After: Touchscreen drivers are compiled as kernel modules.  An init script is used during boot to load each one in a specified order until a touchscreen device is detected.  The atmel max touch driver used by the GRS7 hardware rev with part number P2594VNC7C11 will be attempted first.  And the gpio reset will not be used for the driver.  Using the gpio reset was determined to cause the issue.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

rca_review_comments: A software design defect was identified in the Nurse Call system's handling of dome lights and zone lights on RCB2 hardware. Following a reboot or power cycle of a room containing both a dome light and a zone light, call-tone associations could become incorrectly initialized. As a result, Code Blue (and other configured) calls placed from a zoned room triggered audible tones on an unrelated dome light, even though the dome light did not illuminate and the zone light functioned as configured. The condition persisted until a call was placed from the rebooted room, which restored the correct call-tone mapping. The issue was reproducible across multiple floors at Stanford 500P Hospital and was documented under defect **CWS-BUG-2109**

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.
